extraction.name: NeedleBench
extraction.description: NeedleBench is a comprehensive synthetic benchmark framework for evaluating LLM retrieval and reasoning in bilingual long-context tasks with adaptive context lengths (4k, 8k, 32k, 128k, 200k, 1000k, and beyond). It includes information-sparse tasks (Single-Needle Retrieval, Multi-Needle Retrieval, Multi-Needle Reasoning) and an information-dense task called the Ancestral Trace Challenge (ATC). The framework systematically embeds key data points at varying depths to rigorously test models' capabilities in diverse settings.
extraction.creator: Mo Li, Songyang Zhang, Taolin Zhang, Haodong Duan, Yunxin Liu, Kai Chen
extraction.rai:dataCollection: The dataset is programmatically constructed using a systematic algorithmic approach to generate synthetic family relationship datasets. The generation process involves randomly sampling unique names, assigning relationship terms, generating diverse relationship descriptions using predefined linguistic templates, shuffling relationship statements, creating question prompts, and computing ground truth answers. Haystack content for English tasks uses passages from the PaulGrahamEssays dataset, and for Chinese tasks, the ChineseDomainModelingEval dataset is used.
extraction.rai:dataCollectionRawData: The haystack for English tasks is built using passages from the PaulGrahamEssays dataset, and for Chinese tasks, the ChineseDomainModelingEval dataset is used. The needles are synthetic, fictional statements and kinship relations generated algorithmically.
extraction.rai:dataBiases: The benchmark is synthetic and may not fully reflect the complexity of real-world tasks. Additionally, real-world text benchmarks risk evaluating memorization due to potential pre-training data overlap.
extraction.rai:dataLimitations: NeedleBench is synthetic and may not fully reflect real-world task complexity. Existing benchmarks that use irrelevant filler content may allow models to succeed by focusing on a few key points without truly reading the full context. Real-world benchmarks risk evaluating memorization due to pre-training data overlap.
extraction.rai:dataSocialImpact: The dataset supports evaluation of LLMs for high-stakes applications such as legal document retrieval, academic research, and business intelligence aggregation, where accurate long-context understanding is critical.
extraction.rai:dataUseCases: NeedleBench is designed for evaluating (testing/benchmarking) LLMs on retrieval and reasoning tasks in long-context scenarios, supporting flexible context lengths (4k, 8k, 32k, 128k, 200k, 1000k and beyond). It covers both information-sparse tasks (Single-Needle Retrieval, Multi-Needle Retrieval, Multi-Needle Reasoning) and information-dense tasks (Ancestral Trace Challenge). It is intended to provide a comprehensive, targeted assessment of models' abilities to extract, analyze, and reason over long texts.
extraction.rai:dataReleaseMaintenancePlan: All reproducible scripts, code, and datasets will be made available upon publication.
extraction.rai:dataManipulationProtocol: Synthetic ATC data generation with name randomization, relationship template variation, shuffling of relationship statements to eliminate positional bias, scalable needle counts (2-512), and bilingual support
extraction.rai:dataPreprocessingProtocol: ATC instances generated through: randomly sampling unique names to form a sequential family chain, assigning relationship terms with generation weights, generating diverse relationship descriptions using predefined linguistic templates, shuffling relationship statements, creating question prompts based on question type, and computing ground truth answers

rai:dataCollection.evidence: The algorithm generates each ATC instance through six key steps: (1) randomly sampling n + 1 unique names to form a sequential family chain, (2) assigning relationship terms with corresponding generation weights, (3) generating diverse relationship descriptions using predefined linguistic templates, (4) shuffling all relationship statements to eliminate positional bias, (5) creating question prompts based on the specified question type, and (6) computing ground truth answers according to the constructed family structure.

rai:dataCollectionType.evidence: These tasks are largely synthetic... The needles are synthetic, abstract, and fictional statements or relational facts, deliberately designed to avoid overlap with any real-world knowledge or pretraining data.

rai:dataCollectionRawData.evidence: The haystack for English tasks is built by extending the prompt with passages from the PaulGrahamEssays dataset (Kamradt, 2023), and for Chinese tasks, we use the ChineseDomainModelingEval dataset (Wei et al., 2023b) to ensure linguistic diversity and high-quality filler content.

rai:dataBiases.evidence: NeedleBench is a synthetic benchmark and may not fully reflect the complexity of real-world tasks.

rai:dataLimitations.evidence: NeedleBench is a synthetic benchmark and may not fully reflect the complexity of real-world tasks... inserting too much irrelevant content can make it easy for models to complete tasks by focusing only on a few key points, without truly reading the full context.

rai:dataSocialImpact.evidence: LLMs can rapidly identify and summarize relevant information within lengthy documents, making them invaluable for legal document retrieval, academic research, and aggregating business intelligence, among other applications.

rai:dataUseCases.evidence: NeedleBench, a dataset framework that encompasses both information-sparse and information-dense tasks. NeedleBench is designed to provide a comprehensive, targeted assessment of models' abilities to extract, analyze, and reason over long texts.

rai:dataReleaseMaintenancePlan.evidence: All reproducible scripts, code, and datasets will be made available upon publication.

rai:dataManipulationProtocol.evidence: name randomization prevents memorization, relationship template variation creates linguistic diversity, four question types evaluate different reasoning aspects, needle counts from 2 to 512 provide scalable complexity, and bilingual support enables cross-language evaluation

rai:dataPreprocessingProtocol.evidence: The algorithm generates each ATC instance through six key steps: (1) randomly sampling n + 1 unique names to form a sequential family chain, (2) assigning relationship terms with corresponding generation weights (1 for parent-child, 2 for grandparent-grandchild), (3) generating diverse relationship descriptions using predefined linguistic templates, (4) shuffling all relationship statements to eliminate positional bias, (5) creating question prompts based on the specified question type, and (6) computing ground truth answers according to the constructed family structure.
